title: Pianos and picky pianist Lloyd Glenn
summary: Dance halls usually had pianos, but Lloyd Glenn refused to play instruments too low in pitch, so the band sometimes played without piano. A brief break for phone and coffee chatter intervenes.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Oh, yes, I have worlds of scrapbooks. Do you want to get the picture to you? I think she got it. Okay. All right. Let's see. Well, back to business of just how you would get set up and everything. Did you ever have to rent pianos in those days?

No, usually the dance halls had them in there, but I had a very, very peculiar pianist. To me, he's one of the greatest, and you know who I'm referring to, Lloyd Glenn. And he was very picky about his pianos. And a lot of times we'd come to these dance halls, and the pianos were so low that we would have to tune up with the piano and change our whole way of playing. Because we couldn't reach the piano, or narrow to tune it. So if we tune with the piano, Lloyd Glenn would have to transpose maybe a tone or two above where we were playing. He didn't want that. And he just wouldn't play, so we'd play without a piano. Do you want him on the phone?
That was wonderful, not on the other phone. Oh, I see. I didn't answer upstairs. Yeah, well, we can turn it off for a second.
Sorry, man, I like this. It's skim milk. Oh, well, that's good for me.
It seems as though my brother-in-law has to be on the diet and he has to have skim milk.
Oh, thank you, Mr. Hollins. We were talking about the pianos and how he didn't want to... Right. ...dine's pose.
He wouldn't play on it, Dick. He was picky.
Yeah. And so you couldn't retune him, you just were there.
Oh, the band would just go ahead with us. Yeah, I know that.
What about... Oh, you would get your chords from another instrument, maybe?
Well, from the guitar or the banjo.
